sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy cements its absolute leadership as the market's sole "all-green" sector, while Technology shows the only upward mobility in an otherwise stagnant tape.

Energy continues to dominate the US sector landscape, standing as the only group with all-green breadth across all time horizons (weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD) and boasting a commanding momentum score of 0.93. Technology is the sole sector showing positive rotation, gaining one spot to rank second with a strong momentum score of 0.72, joining Healthcare (momentum 0.72) in the leading tier.

Conversely, defensive and cyclical laggards continue to drag, with Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.20) and Communication Services (momentum 0.25) pinned to the bottom of the rankings. Basic Materials and Real Estate are fading, both slipping one spot over the last five sessions, though Basic Materials retains a top-five momentum profile despite the minor slip.

## Strength
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy is the single "all-green" sector out of 11 groups, showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD with a top-ranked momentum score of 0.93.
* **Sustained Leadership:** Energy remains firmly anchored as a top-three performer across 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month horizons.
* **Top-Tier Chasers:** Healthcare (Rank 4) and Technology (Rank 2) follow Energy as key pillars of strength, both holding momentum scores of 0.72.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Technology Gains Ground:** Technology was the sole positive mover over the last five sessions, improving by +1 spot to reach Rank 2 with 0.72 momentum.
* **Materials and Real Estate Slip:** Basic Materials (Rank 3, momentum 0.58) and Real Estate (Rank 6, momentum 0.40) were the week's top losers, each dropping 1 spot.
* **Persistent Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical remains the weakest sector in the market, sitting at Rank 11 with a momentum score of just 0.20, closely followed by Utilities at 0.23 (Rank 9) and Communication Services at 0.25 (Rank 10).

## Divergences
* **No Fragile All-Green Signals:** No early-warning fragile divergences were detected in the data, confirming the structural integrity of Energy's clean sweep across all timeframes.
* **Financials Positive Divergence:** Financials (Rank 7) show a positive momentum divergence at 0.63, outstripping the momentum of the higher-ranked Basic Materials (Rank 3, momentum 0.58).
* **Industrials Momentum Deficit:** Industrials maintain a mid-pack Rank 5 but exhibit a negative divergence with a weak underlying momentum score of 0.37, placing it among the market's momentum laggards.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and shipping dominate the market's narrow leadership, while consumer electronics and coal surge as travel and precious metals experience sharp pullbacks.

The market exhibits narrow breadth, with only 10 of 144 industry groups achieving "all-green" status across all timeframes. Energy remains the undisputed leader, anchored by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.986) and Oil & Gas Integrated (momentum 0.865), alongside Marine Shipping (momentum 0.875). Simultaneously, we are seeing a sharp rotation into Consumer Electronics (+22 spots, rank 37) and coal industries (Coking Coal +21, Thermal Coal +21), indicating selective cyclical and tech demand.

In contrast, defensive and travel-related areas are fading rapidly. Textile Manufacturing (-33 spots), Uranium (-30 spots), and Travel Services (-25 spots) led the weekly declines, while Gold (-21 spots) also pulled back. Early-warning signals show emerging interest in defensive laggards like Utilities - Regulated Gas (+14 spots, momentum 0.43) and Discount Stores (+12 spots, momentum 0.44), while previously strong groups like Biotechnology and Copper are beginning to slip in rank.

## Strength
* **Narrow Breadth:** Only 10 of 144 industry groups are all-green across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons.
* **Energy Dominance:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing leads all groups with a momentum score of 0.986 (YTD rank 2), followed closely by Oil & Gas Integrated (momentum 0.865) and Oil & Gas E&P (momentum 0.850).
* **Sustained Leaders:** Marine Shipping (momentum 0.875) and Health Information Services (momentum 0.852) remain firmly in the top tier of sustained performers across 1-, 3-, and 6-month rankings.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Consumer Electronics jumped 22 spots to rank 37 (momentum 0.83), while Coking Coal and Thermal Coal both surged 21 spots to ranks 42 and 63, respectively.
* **Sharp Decliners:** Textile Manufacturing plunged 33 spots (rank 64, momentum 0.20), Uranium fell 30 spots (rank 85, momentum 0.34), and Travel Services dropped 25 spots (rank 113, momentum 0.38).
* **Deep Laggards:** Airports & Air Services (momentum 0.062), Footwear & Accessories (momentum 0.070), and Mortgage Finance (momentum 0.078) continue to anchor the bottom of the YTD rankings.

## Divergences
* **Fading Momentum:** Several high-momentum groups are losing ground, led by Other Industrial Metals & Mining (momentum 0.63, rank -6 over 5 days), Copper (momentum 0.66, rank -5), and Biotechnology (momentum 0.81, rank -4).
* **Emerging Laggards:** Underperforming groups with low momentum are starting to climb the ranks, notably Utilities - Regulated Gas (+14 spots, momentum 0.43), Discount Stores (+12 spots, momentum 0.44), and Utilities - Diversified (+10 spots, momentum 0.42).
